subproblem.title: Mass upper bound M_W(T) ≤ μ(W) for a representation with |ξ(x)(α)| ≤ |α| (parent step 10)
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P, T ∈ 𝒟_n(U) (GeometricCurrentOn U n), μ a measure on ℝ^P and ξ : ℝ^P → Λ_n (MultiVector P n). Assume |ξ(x)(α)| ≤ covectorEuclideanNorm α for every x and every n-covector α, and T(ω) = ∫ ξ(x)(ω(x)) dμ(x) (Bochner integral) for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U). Then M_W(T) = T.massOn W ≤ μ(W) for every set W ⊆ ℝ^P.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (T : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (μ : Measure (Euclid P)) (ξ : Euclid P → MultiVector P n), (∀ (x : Euclid P) (α : Covector (Euclid P) n), |ξ x α| ≤ covectorEuclideanNorm α) → (∀ ω : TestFormOn U n, T ω = ∫ x, ξ x ((ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) x) ∂μ) → ∀ W : Set (Euclid P), T.massOn W ≤ μ W
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof, step 10. The bound is proved for every set W; the parent needs only open W. The case μ(W) = ∞ needs no separate treatment.
Notation: |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α. By definition (Simon 6.2.5; SimonGMT GeometricCurrentOn.massOn), M_W(T) is the supremum in [0, ∞] of ofReal(T ω) over ω ∈ massAdmissibleOn U n W. Such ω are exactly the ω ∈ TestFormOn U n with tsupport ω ⊆ W and |ω(x)| ≤ 1 for every x.
1. By sSup_le it suffices to show ofReal(T ω) ≤ μ(W) for every admissible ω. Fix one, and put K := tsupport ω and f(x) := ξ(x)(ω(x)). K is closed, hence Borel, and T(ω) = ∫ f dμ by hypothesis.
2. (Pointwise bound.) For x ∈ K, |f(x)| ≤ |ω(x)| ≤ 1. For x ∉ K, ω(x) = 0 (image_eq_zero_of_notMem_tsupport), hence f(x) = ξ(x)(0) = 0. So ‖f(x)‖ₑ ≤ 1_K(x) for every x.
3. (Chain.) ofReal(T ω) = ofReal(∫ f dμ) ≤ ofReal|∫ f dμ| = ‖∫ f dμ‖ₑ (Real.enorm_eq_ofReal_abs).
 - ‖∫ f dμ‖ₑ ≤ ∫⁻ ‖f‖ₑ dμ (enorm_integral_le_lintegral_enorm). This holds for every f, integrable or not, and needs no measurability of ξ.
 - ∫⁻ ‖f‖ₑ dμ ≤ ∫⁻ 1_K dμ = μ(K), by step 2 and lintegral_indicator_one (K measurable).
 - μ(K) ≤ μ(W), since K ⊆ W.
4. Taking the supremum over admissible ω gives M_W(T) ≤ μ(W). ∎
proof_key_steps: Reduce to ofReal(T ω) ≤ μ(W) for each ω ∈ massAdmissibleOn U n W (sSup_le).
|ξ(x)(ω(x))| ≤ |ω(x)| ≤ 1 on tsupport ω, and ξ(x)(ω(x)) = 0 off tsupport ω.
ofReal(∫ f dμ) ≤ ‖∫ f dμ‖ₑ ≤ ∫⁻ ‖f‖ₑ dμ ≤ μ(tsupport ω) ≤ μ(W).

audit.reason: The stronger conclusion for arbitrary W is valid and matches the prose. Each admissible evaluation is bounded by the integral of the indicator of its closed support, then by μ(W). The unconditional integral-norm inequality justifies omitting measurability assumptions on ξ. Taking the defining supremum proves the exact statement.

subproblem.title: Exhaustion of W ∩ U by compactly contained open sets (parent step 12)
subproblem.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ, let μ be a measure on ℝ^P, let U, W ⊆ ℝ^P be open with μ(ℝ^P ∖ U) = 0, and let m ∈ [0, ∞]. Suppose μ(W') ≤ m for every open W' with W' ⊂⊂ U (CompactlyContained W' U: closure W' is compact and contained in U) and W' ⊆ W. Then μ(W) ≤ m.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (μ : Measure (Euclid P)) (U W : Set (Euclid P)) (m : ℝ≥0∞), IsOpen U → IsOpen W → μ Uᶜ = 0 → (∀ W' : Set (Euclid P), IsOpen W' → CompactlyContained W' U → W' ⊆ W → μ W' ≤ m) → μ W ≤ m
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof, step 12. The exhaustion uses the extended distance infEDist instead of infDist, so the case O = ℝ^P, where Oᶜ = ∅ and infEDist(·, ∅) = ∞, needs no separate treatment.
1. O := W ∩ U is open. W ⊆ O ∪ Uᶜ, so μ(W) ≤ μ(O) + μ(Uᶜ) = μ(O) (measure_union_le and μ(Uᶜ) = 0).
2. For j ∈ ℕ define W'_j := {y : ‖y‖ < j and (j+1)⁻¹ < infEDist(y, Oᶜ)} and F_j := {y : ‖y‖ ≤ j and (j+1)⁻¹ ≤ infEDist(y, Oᶜ)}. Here (j+1)⁻¹ ∈ (0, ∞) is computed in [0, ∞].
3. W'_j is open and F_j is closed. The maps y ↦ ‖y‖ and y ↦ infEDist(y, Oᶜ) are continuous (continuous_infEDist). A strict inequality between continuous functions defines an open set (isOpen_lt), and a non-strict one a closed set (isClosed_le). Since W'_j ⊆ F_j, closure W'_j ⊆ F_j (closure_minimal).
4. F_j ⊆ closedBall(0, j), which is compact because ℝ^P is proper. So F_j and its closed subset closure W'_j are compact (IsCompact.of_isClosed_subset).
5. F_j ⊆ O. If y ∈ F_j and y ∉ O, then y ∈ Oᶜ, so infEDist(y, Oᶜ) = 0 (infEDist_zero_of_mem) < (j+1)⁻¹, a contradiction.
6. So closure W'_j is compact and closure W'_j ⊆ O ⊆ U, i.e. CompactlyContained W'_j U. Also W'_j ⊆ closure W'_j ⊆ O ⊆ W. By hypothesis, μ(W'_j) ≤ m for every j.
7. The sequence (W'_j) is increasing: for j ≤ k, ‖y‖ < j ≤ k and (k+1)⁻¹ ≤ (j+1)⁻¹.
8. ⋃_j W'_j = O. The inclusion ⊆ follows from steps 3 and 5. Conversely, let y ∈ O.
 - Oᶜ is closed and y ∉ Oᶜ = closure Oᶜ, so infEDist(y, Oᶜ) ≠ 0 (mem_closure_iff_infEDist_zero).
 - Choose j₁ with (j₁)⁻¹ < infEDist(y, Oᶜ) (ENNReal.exists_inv_nat_lt) and j₂ > ‖y‖ (exists_nat_gt). Put j := max(j₁, j₂).
 - Then ‖y‖ < j₂ ≤ j and (j+1)⁻¹ ≤ (j₁)⁻¹ < infEDist(y, Oᶜ), so y ∈ W'_j.
9. By continuity from below along the increasing sequence (Monotone.measure_iUnion), μ(O) = sup_j μ(W'_j) ≤ m. With step 1, μ(W) ≤ m. ∎
proof_key_steps: W'_j := {‖y‖ < j, infEDist(y, (W∩U)ᶜ) > (j+1)⁻¹} are open, increasing, have compact closures inside W ∩ U, and exhaust W ∩ U.
Continuity from below: μ(W ∩ U) = sup_j μ(W'_j) ≤ m.

audit.reason: The proposition matches the prose. The extended-distance exhaustion is open, increasing, compactly contained in W∩U and exhaustive, including empty and whole-space cases. Continuity from below and μ(Uᶜ)=0 prove the claimed bound without extra finiteness or regularity assumptions.

subproblem.title: Polar normalization of a vector Riesz density and push-forward to ℝ^P (parent steps 4–9)
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n d : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (c : Covector (Euclid P) n ≃L[ℝ] EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)) (μ₀ : Measure U) (ν : U → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)), IsOpen U → (∀ α : Covector (Euclid P) n, covectorEuclideanNorm α = ‖c α‖) → Measurable ν → (∀ K : Set U, IsCompact K → IntegrableOn ν K μ₀) → ∃ (μ : Measure (Euclid P)) (ξ : Euclid P → MultiVector P n) (β : Euclid P → Covector (Euclid P) n), μ Uᶜ = 0 ∧ (∀ K : Set (Euclid P), IsCompact K → K ⊆ U → μ K < ∞) ∧ AEStronglyMeasurable ξ μ ∧ (∀ (x : Euclid P) (α : Covector (Euclid P) n), |ξ x α| ≤ covectorEuclideanNorm α) ∧ AEStronglyMeasurable β μ ∧ (∃ C : ℝ, ∀ x, ‖β x‖ ≤ C) ∧ (∀ x, covectorEuclideanNorm (β x) ≤ 1) ∧ (∀ᵐ x ∂μ, ξ x (β x) = 1) ∧ ∀ ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n, ∫ x, inner ℝ (c (ω x)) (ν x) ∂μ₀ = ∫ x, ξ x (ω x) ∂μ
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof, steps 4–9. These are the polar normalization ρ = |ν|, ν̂ = ν/|ν|, the push-forward μ = val_*(ρμ₀), the fields ξ = ⟨ν̂_e, c(·)⟩ and β = c⁻¹∘ν̂_e, and the identity of step 8. Identity (i) is stated for arbitrary ω because every integral identity in step 8 holds without integrability hypotheses.
Notation: H := ℝ^d = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d) with inner product ⟨·,·⟩; val : ↥U → ℝ^P is the inclusion; |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α.
1. (Polar decomposition.) For x ∈ ↥U put ρ(x) := ‖ν(x)‖ and ν̂(x) := ρ(x)⁻¹ • ν(x), with 0⁻¹ = 0. Both maps are measurable (Measurable.norm, Measurable.inv, Measurable.smul).
 - ν(x) = ρ(x) • ν̂(x) for every x. If ρ(x) = 0, then ν(x) = 0 and both sides vanish. Otherwise ρ(x) • ρ(x)⁻¹ • ν(x) = ν(x).
 - ‖ν̂(x)‖ = 0 if ρ(x) = 0, and ‖ν̂(x)‖ = ρ(x)⁻¹·ρ(x) = 1 otherwise. So ‖ν̂(x)‖ ≤ 1, and ‖ν̂(x)‖ = 1 whenever ρ(x) ≠ 0.
2. (The measure.) U is open, hence measurable, so val is a measurable embedding (MeasurableEmbedding.subtype_coe). Let μ₁ := μ₀.withDensity(x ↦ ofReal ρ(x)) on ↥U and μ := μ₁.map val on ℝ^P.
 - μ(A) = μ₁(val⁻¹A) for every A ⊆ ℝ^P (MeasurableEmbedding.map_apply).
 - ∫ F dμ = ∫ F(val x) dμ₁(x) for every F : ℝ^P → ℝ (MeasurableEmbedding.integral_map).
3. (Unit field on ℝ^P.) Let u := Function.extend val ν̂ 0 : ℝ^P → H, i.e. ν̂ extended by 0.
 - u(val x) = ν̂(x) for x ∈ ↥U (val is injective; Function.Injective.extend_apply), and u(y) = 0 for y ∉ U (Function.extend_apply').
 - u is measurable (MeasurableEmbedding.measurable_extend), and ‖u(y)‖ ≤ 1 for every y by step 1.
4. (Definitions.) ξ(y) := (innerSL ℝ (u y)).comp c, so ξ(y)(α) = ⟨u(y), c(α)⟩. β(y) := c⁻¹(u(y)).
5. (a) val⁻¹(Uᶜ) = ∅, so μ(Uᶜ) = μ₁(∅) = 0.
6. (b) Let K ⊆ U be compact.
 - K is closed, so val⁻¹K is measurable.
 - val⁻¹K is compact in ↥U, because val is inducing and K ⊆ U = range val (Topology.IsInducing.isCompact_preimage_iff).
 - By step 2 and withDensity_apply, μ(K) = μ₁(val⁻¹K) = ∫⁻_{val⁻¹K} ofReal ρ dμ₀ = ∫⁻_{val⁻¹K} ‖ν‖ₑ dμ₀, using ofReal‖v‖ = ‖v‖ₑ. This is finite because ν is μ₀-integrable on the compact set val⁻¹K (HasFiniteIntegral).
7. (c), (e) u is measurable into the second-countable Borel space H, hence strongly measurable (Measurable.stronglyMeasurable). The map v ↦ (innerSL ℝ v).comp c is continuous (Continuous.clm_comp applied to the continuous innerSL ℝ and a constant), and c⁻¹ is continuous. A continuous map composed with a strongly measurable map is strongly measurable (Continuous.comp_stronglyMeasurable). So ξ and β are strongly measurable, in particular μ-a.e. strongly measurable.
8. (d) For all y and α: |ξ(y)(α)| = |⟨u(y), c α⟩| ≤ ‖u(y)‖·‖c α‖ ≤ ‖c α‖ = |α|. This uses Cauchy–Schwarz (abs_real_inner_le_norm), ‖u(y)‖ ≤ 1 and the hypothesis on c.
9. (f) Let C := ‖c⁻¹‖, the operator norm of c⁻¹ as a continuous linear map H → Λⁿ. Then ‖β(y)‖ ≤ ‖c⁻¹‖·‖u(y)‖ ≤ C (ContinuousLinearMap.le_opNorm).
10. (g) |β(y)| = ‖c(c⁻¹(u(y)))‖ = ‖u(y)‖ ≤ 1.
11. (h) ξ(y)(β(y)) = ⟨u(y), c(c⁻¹(u(y)))⟩ = ⟨u(y), u(y)⟩ = ‖u(y)‖². So {y : ξ(y)(β(y)) ≠ 1} ⊆ Z := {y : ‖u(y)‖ ≠ 1}, a measurable set, and it suffices to show μ(Z) = 0.
 - By step 2, μ(Z) = μ₁(val⁻¹Z).
 - The density is measurable, so by withDensity_apply_eq_zero, μ₁(val⁻¹Z) = 0 iff μ₀({x : ofReal ρ(x) ≠ 0} ∩ val⁻¹Z) = 0.
 - This set is empty. If ofReal ρ(x) ≠ 0, then ρ(x) ≠ 0, so ‖u(val x)‖ = ‖ν̂(x)‖ = 1 by steps 1 and 3, i.e. val x ∉ Z.
12. (i) Let ω : ℝ^P → Λⁿ be arbitrary.
 - By step 2, ∫ ξ(y)(ω(y)) dμ(y) = ∫ ξ(val x)(ω(val x)) dμ₁(x).
 - The density x ↦ ofReal ρ(x) is measurable and finite everywhere, so integral_withDensity_eq_integral_toReal_smul gives = ∫ (ofReal ρ(x)).toReal·ξ(val x)(ω(val x)) dμ₀(x). Since ρ ≥ 0 and by step 3, this is ∫ ρ(x)·⟨ν̂(x), c(ω(val x))⟩ dμ₀(x).
 - Pointwise, by step 1, inner_smul_right and symmetry of the real inner product: ⟨c(ω(val x)), ν(x)⟩ = ⟨c(ω(val x)), ρ(x)•ν̂(x)⟩ = ρ(x)·⟨ν̂(x), c(ω(val x))⟩.
 - So the two integrands agree at every point of ↥U, and ∫_{↥U} ⟨c(ω(x)), ν(x)⟩ dμ₀(x) = ∫ ξ(y)(ω(y)) dμ(y).
 - Every identity used holds for arbitrary integrands, since the Bochner integral of a non-integrable function is 0 on both sides. So no hypothesis on ω is needed. ∎
Lean note: keep μ₁ visible as μ₀.withDensity (fun x => ENNReal.ofReal (ρ x)), for example via an rfl equation, before rewriting with withDensity_apply, withDensity_apply_eq_zero or integral_withDensity_eq_integral_toReal_smul. A let-bound name does not match these lemma patterns syntactically.
proof_key_steps: Polar decomposition ν = ρ•ν̂ with ρ = ‖ν‖; ‖ν̂‖ ≤ 1 everywhere and ‖ν̂‖ = 1 where ρ ≠ 0.
μ := (μ₀.withDensity (ofReal∘ρ)).map val, with val a measurable embedding since U is open; u := ν̂ extended by 0.
ξ(y) := ⟨u(y), c(·)⟩ and β := c⁻¹∘u. Then (a)–(g) follow from val⁻¹(Uᶜ) = ∅, compactness of val⁻¹K, local integrability of ν, continuity and Cauchy–Schwarz.
(h): ξ(β) = ‖u‖², and μ{‖u‖ ≠ 1} = 0 by withDensity_apply_eq_zero, because ρ = 0 wherever ‖ν̂‖ ≠ 1.
(i): integral_map, then integral_withDensity_eq_integral_toReal_smul, then the pointwise identity ⟨c ω, ρν̂⟩ = ρ⟨ν̂, c ω⟩.

audit.reason: All nine conclusions and hypotheses match the elaborated proposition. Measurable normalization, zero extension, weighted push-forward, compact-set integrability, dual bounds and the operator-norm bound on β are justified. The weighted measure annihilates the zero-density obstruction to ξ(β)=1. Both integral transformations apply to arbitrary integrands with the stated measurable, finite density. The intended dual construction checks using c.toContinuousLinearMap; this is a routine projection in formalization.

subproblem.title: Test forms in U restrict to compactly supported continuous maps on the subspace U
subproblem.statement: Let P, n, d ∈ ℕ and let U ⊆ ℝ^P be an arbitrary set with the subspace topology (the subtype ↥U). Let f : Λⁿ(ℝ^P) → ℝ^d (Covector (Euclid P) n → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)) be continuous with f(0) = 0. Let ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) (TestFormOn U n): a C^∞ n-form on ℝ^P with compact support and tsupport ω ⊆ U. Then there is g ∈ C_c(U, ℝ^d) (CompactlySupportedContinuousMap ↥U (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d))) with g(x) = f(ω(x)) for every x ∈ U.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n d : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (f : Covector (Euclid P) n → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)), Continuous f → f 0 = 0 → ∀ ω : TestFormOn U n, ∃ g : CompactlySupportedContinuousMap U (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)), ∀ x : U, g x = f ((ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) x)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof, step 8, first sentence (g_ω(x) := c(ω(val x)) is continuous, with support in the compact set val⁻¹(tsupport ω)). It is stated here for any continuous f with f(0) = 0; the parent uses f := c.
Notation: val : ↥U → ℝ^P is the inclusion and K := tsupport ω.
1. Membership ω ∈ TestFormOn U n means IsTestForm ω and K ⊆ U, where IsTestForm ω means that ω is C^∞ and HasCompactSupport ω. So ω is continuous (ContDiff.continuous) and K is compact.
2. Define G : ↥U → ℝ^d by G(x) := f(ω(val x)). G is continuous, being the composition of the continuous maps val (continuous_subtype_val), ω and f.
3. K_U := val⁻¹(K) is compact in ↥U. The map val is inducing (Topology.IsInducing.subtypeVal) and K ⊆ U = range val (Subtype.range_coe). So by Topology.IsInducing.isCompact_preimage_iff, val⁻¹(K) is compact iff K is, and K is compact by step 1.
4. If x ∈ ↥U and x ∉ K_U, then val x ∉ tsupport ω, so ω(val x) = 0 (image_eq_zero_of_notMem_tsupport). Hence G(x) = f(0) = 0.
5. ↥U is Hausdorff, as a subspace of the metric space ℝ^P. By steps 3–4 and HasCompactSupport.intro, G has compact support.
6. Let g ∈ C_c(U, ℝ^d) be the element with underlying continuous map G (steps 2 and 5). For every x ∈ U, g(x) = G(x) = f(ω(x)) by definition (rfl). ∎
proof_key_steps: G := f ∘ ω ∘ val is continuous.
val⁻¹(tsupport ω) is compact, because val is inducing and tsupport ω ⊆ U = range val.
G vanishes off val⁻¹(tsupport ω) since f(0) = 0, so G has compact support (HasCompactSupport.intro); package it as g ∈ C_c(U, ℝ^d).

audit.reason: The one-line proposition matches all prose hypotheses. The support lies in U, so its preimage under the subtype embedding is compact even for arbitrary U. Continuity and f(0)=0 then give the required compactly supported continuous map. The supplied construction proves the exact conclusion without another child.

subproblem.title: Mass lower bound μ(W') ≤ M_W(T) on compactly contained open W' ⊆ W via a norming field (parent step 11)
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (T : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (μ : Measure (Euclid P)) (ξ : Euclid P → MultiVector P n) (β : Euclid P → Covector (Euclid P) n), (∀ K : Set (Euclid P), IsCompact K → K ⊆ U → μ K < ∞) → AEStronglyMeasurable ξ μ → (∀ (x : Euclid P) (α : Covector (Euclid P) n), |ξ x α| ≤ covectorEuclideanNorm α) → (∀ ω : TestFormOn U n, T ω = ∫ x, ξ x ((ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) x) ∂μ) → AEStronglyMeasurable β μ → (∃ C : ℝ, ∀ x, ‖β x‖ ≤ C) → (∀ x, covectorEuclideanNorm (β x) ≤ 1) → (∀ᵐ x ∂μ, ξ x (β x) = 1) → ∀ W W' : Set (Euclid P), IsOpen W' → CompactlyContained W' U → W' ⊆ W → μ W' ≤ T.massOn W
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof, step 11. The facts about μ, ξ and β that step 11 takes from steps 6, 7 and 9 are hypotheses (i)–(viii) here.
Notation: |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α; ν := μ.restrict W'.
1. (Finiteness.) closure W' is compact and contained in U, so μ(W') ≤ μ(closure W') < ∞ by (i). Hence ν is a finite measure, with ν(ℝ^P) = μ(W'). Also ν(W'ᶜ) = μ(W'ᶜ ∩ W') = 0, since W'ᶜ is closed, hence measurable.
2. (β is ν-integrable.) β is ν-a.e. strongly measurable by (v), restricted to W'. It is bounded by C by (vi), and ν is finite (Integrable.of_bound). By (vii), |β(x)| ≤ 1 for ν-a.e. x.
3. (Approximation.) Fix ε > 0. Apply the sibling theorem rsd_mw_exists_testForm_approx (key testform_l1_approx) with P, n, ν, V := W', β, ε. Its hypotheses hold by steps 1–2 and because W' is open. It gives an n-form ω₀ with IsTestForm ω₀, tsupport ω₀ ⊆ W', |ω₀(x)| ≤ 1 for every x, and ∫⁻ ofReal|ω₀(x) − β(x)| dν(x) < ofReal ε.
4. (Admissibility.) tsupport ω₀ ⊆ W' ⊆ closure W' ⊆ U, so ω₀ defines ω ∈ TestFormOn U n. Also tsupport ω ⊆ W' ⊆ W and |ω(x)| ≤ 1, so ω ∈ massAdmissibleOn U n W. Hence ofReal(T ω) ≤ M_W(T) (GeometricCurrentOn.le_massOn).
5. (Localization.) Put f(x) := ξ(x)(ω₀(x)). For x ∉ W' we have x ∉ tsupport ω₀, so ω₀(x) = 0 and f(x) = 0. By (iv) and setIntegral_eq_integral_of_forall_compl_eq_zero, T(ω) = ∫ f dμ = ∫_{W'} f dμ = ∫ f dν.
6. (Integrability.) f is μ-a.e. strongly measurable. Indeed, x ↦ (ξ(x), ω₀(x)) is a.e. strongly measurable by (ii) and continuity of ω₀, and evaluation (L, α) ↦ L(α) is continuous, being bounded bilinear (isBoundedBilinearMap_apply). By (iii), |f(x)| ≤ |ω₀(x)| ≤ 1 for every x. Since ν is finite, f and the constant 1 are ν-integrable.
7. (Pointwise lower bound.) Let h := 1 − f. Then h ≥ 0 everywhere, since f ≤ 1. By (viii) restricted to W', ξ(x)(β(x)) = 1 for ν-a.e. x. For such x, linearity of ξ(x) and (iii) give f(x) = ξ(x)(β(x)) + ξ(x)(ω₀(x) − β(x)) = 1 + ξ(x)(ω₀(x) − β(x)) ≥ 1 − |ω₀(x) − β(x)|. That is, h(x) ≤ |ω₀(x) − β(x)| for ν-a.e. x.
8. (Integral of h.) h ≥ 0 and h is ν-a.e. strongly measurable, so ∫ h dν = (∫⁻ ofReal h dν).toReal (integral_eq_lintegral_of_nonneg_ae). By steps 7 and 3, ∫⁻ ofReal h dν ≤ ∫⁻ ofReal|ω₀ − β| dν < ofReal ε (lintegral_mono_ae). Hence ∫ h dν < ε (ENNReal.toReal_lt_of_lt_ofReal).
9. (Lower bound for T(ω).) By integral_sub and integral_const, ∫ h dν = ∫ 1 dν − ∫ f dν = μ.real(W') − ∫ f dν, since ν(ℝ^P) = μ(W'). Therefore T(ω) = ∫ f dν = μ.real(W') − ∫ h dν > μ.real(W') − ε.
10. (Fixed ε.) μ(W') = ofReal(μ.real W'), as μ(W') < ∞. Then μ(W') ≤ ofReal(μ.real W' − ε) + ofReal ε (ENNReal.ofReal_add_le) ≤ ofReal(T ω) + ofReal ε ≤ M_W(T) + ofReal ε, by steps 9 and 4.
11. ε > 0 was arbitrary, so μ(W') ≤ M_W(T) (ENNReal.le_of_forall_pos_le_add). ∎
proof_key_steps: ν := μ.restrict W' is finite (closure W' is a compact subset of U), ν(W'ᶜ) = 0, and β is ν-integrable with |β| ≤ 1.
rsd_mw_exists_testForm_approx gives a unit test form ω₀ with tsupport ω₀ ⊆ W' and ∫⁻ ofReal|ω₀ − β| dν < ofReal ε; ω₀ is admissible for M_W(T).
T(ω₀) = ∫_{W'} ξ(ω₀) dμ, and ξ(ω₀) ≥ 1 − |ω₀ − β| ν-a.e., because ξ(β) = 1 a.e. and |ξ(α)| ≤ |α|.
Hence T(ω₀) > μ.real(W') − ε, so μ(W') ≤ M_W(T) + ε for every ε > 0.

audit.reason: All eight hypotheses and support conditions match the proposition. Compact containment makes the restricted measure finite; the explicit operator-norm bound makes β integrable. The correctly declared approximation dependency supplies an admissible form. Continuous evaluation gives integrability, normalization bounds the nonnegative error, and the ε-limit yields μ(W') ≤ T.massOn W. No parent conclusion is assumed.
